next.name: Threat Group-3390
next.headline: Threat Group-3390: a long-tracked China-nexus group with a well-known toolkit
next.in_short: Threat Group-3390 goes by many names, including APT27, Emissary Panda and Iron Tiger. Public reports list a deep toolkit, and Google's threat team describes the group as PRC-nexus.

sentences.t: MITRE tracks this actor as Threat Group-3390. It is also known as Earth Smilodon, TG-3390, Emissary Panda, BRONZE UNION, APT27, Iron Tiger, LuckyMouse and Linen Typhoon.
Google Threat Intelligence Group describes APT27 as a PRC-nexus threat actor.
The catalogue lists many remote access tools for this group, including PlugX, HyperBro, gh0st RAT, ZxShell, RCSession, SysUpdate and Clambling.
It also lists the web shells China Chopper and ASPXSpy, and the frameworks Cobalt Strike and Impacket.
For stealing credentials, the catalogue names Mimikatz, gsecdump, pwdump and Windows Credential Editor.
The catalogue also lists built-in Windows tools such as Systeminfo, Tasklist, netstat, ipconfig and certutil, along with the scanner NBTscan.

Recorded Future's Insikt Group lists LuckyMouse, a name for this group, among the actors that have used Scanbox in the past. Scanbox is a reconnaissance framework written in JavaScript and PHP that can log keystrokes.

A threat report titled "Iron Tiger Compromises Chat Application Mimi, Targets Windows, Mac, and Linux Users" lists indicators for the campaign. They include HyperBro samples for Windows and Rshell samples for Linux and Mac OS.
The page is mostly a list of indicators. It gives no account of who was targeted or when.
Google Threat Intelligence Group says it saw APT27 activity in which the actor used Gemini. It also says an APT27 fleet management application is likely to support an ORB network.
Treat tool names and indicator lists as a starting point for detection. They do not show the full scope of an intrusion.
